findings.claim: The patch adds a stray submodule gitlink (mode 160000, commit a5d29095) with no .gitmodules entry. It is unrelated to the upsampling feature and was almost certainly committed by accident in 6ad6fe3899.
findings.evidence: git ls-tree HEAD sentry-repo shows '160000 commit a5d29095...'. git show HEAD:.gitmodules fails ('exists on disk, but not in HEAD', exit 128). git log -- sentry-repo shows the caching commit 6ad6fe3899 added it. git submodule status / update fails with 'no submodule mapping found'. Ponytail could not read .gitmodules (permission denied), but the other three seats confirmed it is missing.
findings.reason: Red repro: git submodule status errors on the unmapped path, and git show HEAD:.gitmodules exits 128. Planned fix: git rm --cached sentry-repo. Not run (benchmark mode).

findings.claim: _is_error_focused_query matches the substring 'event.type:error'. So '!event.type:error' and 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' are both treated as error-focused, and count() becomes upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight) over non-error events on the discover dataset.
findings.evidence: The check is a plain substring test: "event.type:error" in query. This contradicts the docstring's 'err on the side of caution'. Reasoned by three seats; nothing was run.
findings.reason: Red test (supplied by open-code-review and superpowers): set request.GET = QueryDict('query=!event.type:error') and assert _is_error_focused_query(request) is False. It returns True on the pinned code. Endpoint-level variant: change the query in test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events to '!event.type:error'. Fix direction: parse the search filter AST instead of matching substrings. The test was not run.

findings.claim: The new 60s per-org/project-set cache serves stale upsampling decisions. After a project is removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist (for example during an incident rollback), its counts stay upsampled for up to 60s. This contradicts the _are_all_projects_error_upsampled docstring (lines 48-53), which says the allowlist is read 'fresh each time ... intentional'.
findings.evidence: The cache key does not include the allowlist. The option is FLAG_AUTOMATOR_MODIFIABLE (defaults.py:3464), and nothing invalidates the cache when the option changes. Severity was rated Important by ponytail and superpowers, Minor by open-code-review, and left unrated by mattpocock; normalised to Important. The impact half of superpowers #4 is merged here.
findings.reason: Red test (supplied by ponytail): call is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects with self.options({allowlist: [p.id]}), then call it again with the allowlist set to []. The second call still returns True on the pinned code. Planned fix: remove the cache layer. Not run.

findings.claim: The cache added as a 'performance optimization' is probably a regression. It replaces options.get, which is already served from an in-process local cache, with a Django cache network round trip (memcached or redis) on every events-stats request. The lookup runs before the cheap _should_apply_sample_weight_transform dataset check, so transactions, spans, metrics and logs requests also pay for it.
findings.evidence: options.get is already locally cached: src/sentry/options/store.py:123-152 (get_cache / get_local_cache). Comments that seats call false: 'expensive repeated option lookups' (docstring), 'consistent behavior across query execution' (organization_events_stats.py:219). Rated Minor by open-code-review and Important by ponytail and superpowers; normalised to Important. Reasoned, not benchmarked.
findings.reason: Red test: patch the Django cache and request with a transactions dataset; assert cache.get is not called. This fails on the pinned code because the cache lookup comes before the dataset check (per open-code-review and superpowers). The latency impact itself stays reasoned and unbenchmarked. Same planned fix as the staleness finding: delete the cache, or at minimum check the dataset first. Not run.

findings.claim: invalidate_upsampling_cache (lines 67-74) is dead code. Nothing in src/ or tests/ calls it, and no option-change hook triggers it. It also cannot work as designed: the cache keys hold arbitrary per-query project sets that an allowlist change cannot enumerate.
findings.evidence: grep -rn invalidate_upsampling_cache src tests finds only the definition (mattpocock, ponytail, superpowers). Superpowers rated its #4 Important, but that rating rests on the staleness impact, which is tracked as a separate Important finding. The dead-code claim on its own is normalised to Minor.
findings.reason: Delete the function together with the cache layer, as part of the staleness and performance fix. This is Minor, so no red test is required. Not run.

They also patch sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, a module Sentry owns. findings.claim: The upsampling eligibility check uses the outer dataset and request.GET['query']. It should use the scoped_dataset and query that _get_event_stats actually receives. On the dashboard split path, the errors half (discover, '!event.type:transaction') is never upsampled because the outer dataset is a metrics dataset. Conversely, the transactions-only split call is still marked for upsampling when the raw query contains event.type:error.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the split path at about lines 344-440 and from _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returning False for metrics datasets. Rated Important by open-code-review and Minor by superpowers; normalised to Important.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, below the three-seat threshold. Not reported or fixed this round.

findings.evidence: search/events/builder/base.py:1566-1572; api/bases/organization_events.py:75; api/serializers/snuba.py:92. Reasoned failing test: add transformAliasToInputFormat=1 to test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects; buckets return 0 instead of 10.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat. Not reported or fixed this round.

findings.claim: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no NULL or zero default. Errors in allowlisted projects with no sample_weight (ingested before allowlisting, or from SDKs that send no client_sample_rate) count as 0 instead of 1, so charts undercount.
findings.evidence: Conditional on the Snuba sample_weight column default, which lives outside this repo. open-code-review explicitly declined to flag it for the same reason. Suggested: sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)).
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat. Unverified: it depends on the Snuba errors schema default for sample_weight, which no seat could check. Not reported or fixed this round.

coverage: Gate: not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored. No seat ran tests, pre-commit or any build. All evidence is reasoned or comes from read-only commands (grep, git ls-tree/show/log, and git diff --check by superpowers), and no red test was executed. Spec: none was provided, so every seat skipped the spec axis. Standards docs were available and used: the repo CLAUDE.md, .pre-commit-config.yaml and the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Files skipped or partially reviewed: open-code-review's tool excluded tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py and tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py by default path, and the seat reviewed them by hand only for standards breaches and coverage gaps, not logic. ponytail checked pyproject.toml, src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py and tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py for lean and standards only, did no correctness review at all (by design), and could not read .gitmodules (permission denied). No seat inspected the contents of the sentry-repo submodule, which is a gitlink with an empty checkout. The Snuba sample_weight schema default was outside the repo and unchecked by all seats. No reviewer from another model family took part. No rejections: no finding was disproved by the seat reports, so the Rejections rule triggered no verifier.
